alt: Three routes: AS Level only, taking Components 1 to 3 in one series; A Level staged, with Components 1 to 3 in Year 1 and Component 4 in Year 2; or the full A Level in a single series. Component 4, the Cambridge Research Report, is worth 85 marks, half the full A Level.
caption: Component 4 is the only thing separating the full A Level from the AS.

alt: The four Critical Path stages: deconstruction, reconstruction, reflection, and communication and collaboration. The Written Exam uses deconstruction, reconstruction and communication, but not reflection or collaboration, since it is individual and AO2 Reflection is weighted 0%.
caption: Three stages apply in the exam: take arguments apart, rebuild perspectives, communicate clearly.

alt: An argument broken into the syllabus’s five parts: a conclusion supported by reasons (premises), evidence, assumptions both stated and unstated, and assertions and counter-assertions.
caption: Name the five parts first; judge them second.

alt: Seven structural weaknesses: hasty generalisation, false cause (including confounding variables and reverse causation), false dichotomy, ad hominem, appeal to authority, circular reasoning and straw man, each with a one-line definition.
caption: Look for weak structure, not a conclusion you dislike.

alt: Five tests for evidence: provenance, methodology, currency, corroboration and sufficiency. Below, a rise from 2 cases to 4 is a 100% increase but almost meaningless, showing how percentages can hide small absolute numbers.
caption: Ask whether the evidence can carry the claim, and check the numbers behind any percentage.

alt: The argument that more education spending will raise national income rests only on a correlation. The causal arrow could run in reverse, since richer countries can afford more education, or a confounding variable such as governance, stability or infrastructure could drive both. It also oversimplifies and lacks data on timescale or size of effect.
caption: Name the flaw and show why it breaks the step from evidence to conclusion.
